title: Table caption and summary must differ
summary: A table has a summary attribute that repeats its caption. Remove the duplicate, or make the summary say something different.
problem: A <table> has both a <caption> and a summary attribute with the same text. The two are meant to say different things, so repeating the caption in the summary adds nothing and can be announced twice.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users may hear the same table description twice, which wastes their time on every table that does this.
steps: Find the table in your page that has both a caption and a summary attribute.
Keep the <caption> as the visible title of the table.
Remove the summary attribute, since it is obsolete in HTML5, or make it add information the caption does not.
If a longer explanation is needed, put it in a paragraph next to the table and link it with aria-describedby.

whyItMatters: This is a best practice, not a WCAG failure. Removing the duplicate keeps tables concise for assistive technology users and clears out an obsolete attribute.
howToCheck: Search the page source for summary= on table elements and compare each one with its caption. They should not match, and the summary can usually be removed.
